slice: Triumph TF rider feedback and tests

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tested first on standard 2024 mapping, then on 2025 ECU spec (dealer-updatable). Muffler insert left in with screen cut out.
feedback.observed: Positive: no binding, rear mounts line up with subframe; noticeably stronger corner pull in 2nd and 3rd; more mid-range recovery and longer mid-range than stock; top end slightly improved; quieter and deeper than stock; pull even better on 2025 ECU spec. Negative: stock system has slightly better crack off idle (4.1 mellows initial hit); Megabomb needed some adjustment to line up with engine mount holes; over-rev similar to stock. Cut-screen insert gave better low throttle feel and rear traction.
feedback.measured: Weight savings just over one pound vs stock. Repack every 10-12 hours. Prices: 4.1 Ti muffler $899.99; Megabomb headpipe $475.00.
feedback.other_mods: 13/49 gearing (stock 13/48); 2025 ECU spec; stock headpipe springs reused

feedback.product: Ti-6 Titanium / Ti-6 Pro / T-6 Stainless exhaust system for TF250X
feedback.author: Jody Weisel
feedback.conditions: Product spotlight only; no riding test.
feedback.observed: No tester observations; manufacturer claims only (Ti-6 boosts power and durability; Ti-6 Pro designed for AMA/FIM sound-limited closed-course racing; T-6 lower-cost stainless/aluminum).

feedback.author: Dan Thomerson
feedback.conditions: Accessory-equipped test bike; reviewer weighs 98 kg.
feedback.observed: Louder; more low-mid torque for exiting tight turns and up jump faces.
feedback.measured: Listed (claimed, not measured): 0.47 kg lighter than OE stainless system; claimed power increase from 9,000 to 13,000 rpm.
feedback.other_mods: Optional medium/hard rear springs, gripper seat, XTrig holeshot device, Athena LC-GPA, MX Tune Pro Wi-Fi module fitted or listed

feedback.product: Full exhaust system (on race-spec demo bike) with GET Wi-Fi tuner map
feedback.author: Trent Maher
feedback.conditions: Race-spec demo bike; reviewer 90 kg; stock springs on race-spec bike.
feedback.observed: With race-spec exhaust and map, reviewer could use third gear out of corners.
feedback.other_mods: GET ignition with Wi-Fi tuner, XTrig holeshot device

feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Not tested; mentioned as accessory.
feedback.observed: Not tested. Triumph claims it improves performance, especially at high rpm. Separately, Vital MX and Ultimate Motorcycling note the MX Tune Pro app includes a dedicated Akrapovic map.

feedback.product: RC4 / Podium Flight RC Bend handlebar (TF 450-RC Edition standard)
feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Triumph US racing HQ near Atlanta, GA.
feedback.observed: Narrower and more comfortable than the TF 250-X ProTaper bars; 'a more universal attack position'. 1000PS (Busty Wolter, 1.87 m) also notes bar is slightly narrower than the TF 250-X bar and was comfortable in standard position. Dirt Bike Magazine names it 'ODI Podium Flight RC Bend'; Cycle News calls it 'ODI RC4'; 1000PS 'ODI Signature'.

feedback.product: Gripper seat cover (RC Edition / accessory 'Performance gripper seat')
feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Triumph US racing HQ near Atlanta, GA.
feedback.observed: Helps you stay in place under hard throttle. Bike Review AU (Dan Thomerson, TF 250-X 2024) said the accessory gripper seat helped hold the bike and felt more planted cornering. 1000PS says chosen to reduce arm fatigue.

feedback.author: Jess McKinley
feedback.conditions: Hatfield-McCoy Tornado Single Trax, WV; rain and clay then drying; rider 180 lb.
feedback.observed: Used to keep body in attack position. No further evaluation.

feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.observed: 'A nice touch'; no functional evaluation.

feedback.publication: Cycle News / Bike Review AU / MotoOnline
feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen; Dan Thomerson; Trent Maher
feedback.conditions: Standard on RC Edition; accessory for TF 250-X / TF 450-X.
feedback.observed: No tester evaluated it in use; all mentions are listing-only.

feedback.product: Geomax MX34 (80/100-21, 110/90-19) replacing Pirelli MX32 100 rear
feedback.author: Scott Hoffman / Trevor Hunter
feedback.conditions: Southern California tracks incl. Perris Raceway; ~20 hours; 195-lb rider among testers.
feedback.observed: Swapped to MX34 and 110 rear; chassis felt about the same with either tire.
feedback.other_mods: Pro X 49T rear sprocket, chain +2 links

feedback.product: Scorpion MX32 Mid Soft, 100/90-19 rear (stock) - recommended change to 110 rear
feedback.publication: Keefer Inc Testing (via PulpMX) / MXA / Vital MX / Ultimate Motorcycling
feedback.author: Kris Keefer; MXA staff; Steven Tokarski; Will Embree
feedback.conditions: Keefer: Gatorback FL launch. MXA: Glen Helen etc. Vital: Fox Raceway 2025 model.
feedback.observed: Keefer: MX32 corners well but carcass wears out before knobs and can roll under load; prefers 110 rear; 100 rear partly blamed for bike standing up mid-corner. MXA: 1.85 rear rim with 100/90-19 limits traction. Vital: carcass can fold under load. Ultimate Motorcycling: prefers 110 rear for traction. Dirt Bike Test UK disagrees in effect: chassis felt about the same with either tire.
feedback.measured: Keefer: 14 psi recommended in the Pirellis; a 100 rear is one pound lighter than a 110.

feedback.author: Scott Hoffman / Trevor Hunter
feedback.conditions: Southern California tracks incl. Perris Raceway.
feedback.observed: Fitted to tighten gear spread and use more of third mid-corner. Required chain lengthened two links and axle moved back.

feedback.author: Ron Lawson
feedback.conditions: ~10 hours on bike; Pete Murray raced it at Glen Helen.
feedback.observed: KTM rear sprockets are a 'perfect fit'. Testers disliked stock gearing (gappy 2-3 and 3-4) and planned +2 teeth rear.

feedback.publication: Cycle News / Keefer Inc / Dirt Bike / Dirt Bike Test / MXA
feedback.author: Noah Kepple; Kris Keefer; Ron Lawson; Hoffman/Hunter; MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Various
feedback.observed: DISAGREEMENT: Cycle News (Gatorback launch) said stock 13/48 'felt spot on' but suggested a 49 if 2-3 shifts on hills are inconsistent. Keefer runs 13/49. Dirt Bike planned +2 teeth (13/50). Dirt Bike Test fitted 49. MXA compared stock 13/48 with KTM 250SX-F 13/51 without stating a change.

feedback.product: Optional medium and hard fork/shock springs
feedback.author: Trent Maher
feedback.conditions: Reviewer 90 kg; stock springs rated for 70-80 kg rider; clickers unchanged.
feedback.observed: Stock too soft; medium still soft; hard springs noticeably changed the ride and allowed more aggressive riding. Bike Review AU (Dan Thomerson, 98 kg, stock rated 80 kg) found medium and hard springs gave more confidence on jumps and corners.

feedback.product: Stock KYB AOS fork / shock - clicker and sag settings
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Gatorback Cycle Park, FL launch.
feedback.observed: Bike rides low in corners under load; raised rear. Fork slightly behind YZ250F KYB AOS in bigger bumps; shock wants more damping at end of stroke, high-speed compression helps.
feedback.measured: Shock at 102mm, HSC 7/8 turn out; fork height 3mm, compression two clicks in.

feedback.product: Stock KYB fork / shock - clicker changes
feedback.author: Steven Tokarski
feedback.conditions: Fox Raceway; rider 5'10", 170 lb.
feedback.observed: Stock felt soft and bottomed easily; stock may suit lighter riders; harsh on high-load landings, front less rigid than rear.
feedback.measured: Fork compression +4 clicks stiffer, rebound 3 clicks slower; shock HSC +1/4 turn, LSC +2 clicks, rebound 2 clicks slower (no baseline given).

feedback.product: Stock KYB fork / shock - sag and balance
feedback.author: Scott Hoffman / Trevor Hunter
feedback.conditions: SoCal tracks incl. Perris; rider weights up to 195 lb.
feedback.observed: Fork slightly stiffer than shock; lighter riders softened fork, heavier riders stiffened shock. Fork dives under heavy braking for fast riders. Heavier riders found not bleeding fork air a temporary stiffener. Some wanted a bit more shock compression. Front can feel busy in fast rough corners.
feedback.measured: Race sag ~100-102mm; fast riders +2-3 clicks fork compression; fork height dropped to 3mm on fast tracks.

feedback.publication: Motocross Action / Dirt Bike / Ultimate Motorcycling / Cycle News
feedback.author: MXA staff; Ron Lawson; Will Embree; Noah Kepple
feedback.conditions: Various
feedback.observed: MXA: shock blew through stroke on hard landings/G-outs; stock suited to 155-175 lb; firmed with more low-speed compression and slower rebound on high-traction tracks. Dirt Bike: suspension soft/plush, rear set higher than they usually prefer. Cycle News: went a little stiffer and slower on shock, tried faster fork rebound, returned fork to base; responds well to small changes. Ultimate Motorcycling (160 lb): kept 104mm sag all day, Triumph range 102-105mm.
feedback.measured: Dirt Bike sag ~100mm; Ultimate Motorcycling 104mm; Keefer 102mm. No MXA clicker numbers.

feedback.product: Stock KYB - sag and fork stiffness
feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Triumph US HQ near Atlanta, GA; started at 102mm per Triumph technician.
feedback.observed: Rear felt low at first, front light; lowering sag to 100mm and stiffening forks improved front-end tracking in ruts. Compared feel to Yamaha YZ450F.

feedback.author: Ron Lawson
feedback.conditions: 12-bike 450 comparison.
feedback.observed: Balance and spring rates spot-on for Triumph's 175-lb novice target; pros and riders wanting second-moto roughness may want stiffer; setup sensitive; can feel harsh in rough second motos.
feedback.measured: Best sag 104mm (sensitive to measurement error). Dyno 58.6 hp @ 9200 rpm; 231.3 lb without fuel.

feedback.product: Stock KYB - sag and tire pressure (cross-country)
feedback.author: Jess McKinley; Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Hatfield-McCoy Tornado Single Trax, WV; wet clay then drying.
feedback.observed: Both ran 102mm instead of 105mm standard; Nitzen found more front weight bias improved turning in tight switchbacks. McKinley (180 lb) used full stroke, fork had no wallowing.
feedback.measured: Sag 102mm (both). McKinley tire pressures 12 psi front / 11 psi rear (Dunlop AT82).

feedback.product: MX Tune Pro Wi-Fi module and app (10 preset maps)
feedback.publication: Vital MX / Dirt Bike Test (UK) / Ultimate Motorcycling / Bike Review AU
feedback.author: Steven Tokarski; Hoffman/Hunter; Jess McKinley; Dan Thomerson
feedback.conditions: Various
feedback.observed: Vital: 10 presets (novice-expert, hard pack, loam, sand, Akrapovic) are a nice touch but less tunable than Yamaha's app. Dirt Bike Test: fuel and ignition can't be adjusted directly, tuner required. Cycle News (TF 450-RC): maps are preset, not customizable. Ultimate Motorcycling (TF 450-C): used Soft/Mud map with traction control raised from 3 to 6 of 10; also calls app maps customizable (DISAGREEMENT with Cycle News).
feedback.measured: Price DISAGREEMENT/region: Ultimate Motorcycling $199 (US, 2025-11); Bike Review AU $370 (AUD, 2025-07, TF-E launch).

feedback.author: Kris Keefer; Steven Tokarski
feedback.conditions: Keefer on 2024 bike with FMF 4.1; Vital on 2025 bike.
feedback.observed: Keefer: 2025 ECU spec can be installed by a dealer; pulling power even better with FMF system. Vital: 2025 remap 'eliminates some of the hesitation and mid-range dip' of 2024. MXA (2024) had attributed the low-rpm bog to mapping.

feedback.author: MXA staff; Ron Lawson; Trent Maher
feedback.conditions: Various
feedback.observed: DISAGREEMENT: MXA found map 1 (light off) more aggressive and stronger midrange, same peak; Dirt Bike's favorite was map 2 (light on); MotoOnline saw map 2 as smoother off bottom without losing power, suited to beginners. Dirt Bike: no one defended traction control. TF 450-RC (Cycle News): chose RC/aggressive map; standard map too linear. TF 450-X (Dirt Bike): some prefer mild map's smoothed mid-range; use Quickshift at start then turn off.
feedback.measured: MXA dyno TF250-X: 42.67 hp, 19.65 lb-ft (KTM 250SX-F 44.98 hp, 20.81 lb-ft).

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Glen Helen and National-style track.
feedback.observed: Recommended because stock oil cap sits where a boot can knock it loose.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Glen Helen and National-style track.
feedback.observed: Recommended to keep mud out of footpegs, which collect mud. DISAGREEMENT: Cycle News (Gatorback) said mud never packed the peg pivot.

feedback.publication: Cycle News / MXA / Dirt Bike / Dirt Bike Test
feedback.author: Noah Kepple; MXA staff; Ron Lawson; Hoffman/Hunter
feedback.conditions: Various
feedback.observed: Cycle News: shifter tip may have slop; Triumph said an updated rivet may be in the works. MXA: notchy transmission makes quickshifter practically necessary; QS disengages if lever not fully lifted. Dirt Bike: shifter very stiff on test bike. Dirt Bike Test: light shifter pressure can trigger unexpected upshift. Candidate aftermarket shift lever opportunity; no aftermarket lever tested.

feedback.publication: MXA / Dirt Bike Test / Vital MX
feedback.author: MXA staff; Hoffman/Hunter; Steven Tokarski
feedback.observed: Torx bolts throughout require special tools instead of 8/10mm T-handles (MXA); Dirt Bike Test also complains of 12mm and 13mm nuts. Implies Torx T-handle set as first purchase.

feedback.author: Busty Wolter; Ron Lawson
feedback.conditions: Triumph facility, Georgia USA.
feedback.observed: Chosen for traction; 110 rear width chosen for performance. Standard 2026 TF 450-X reverts to Pirelli MX32 mid-soft (Dirt Bike). No direct comparison ride.

common_first_mods: Set rear sag ~100-104mm (testers ranged 100, 102, 104; Triumph range 102-105mm) and raise the rear / add shock high-speed compression to stop it riding low and bottoming (Keefer, MXA, Dirt Bike Test, Cycle News).
Stiffer springs for riders over ~80 kg (stock rated 70-80 kg per AU tests; MXA says 155-175 lb); Triumph sells medium and hard springs.
Add fork compression (2-4 clicks) and fork height ~3mm for faster riders (Keefer, Vital, Dirt Bike Test).
Gear down one or two teeth (13/49 or 13/50); KTM rear sprockets fit (Dirt Bike).
Swap stock 100/90-19 Pirelli MX32 rear for a 110 (Keefer, Ultimate Motorcycling, Dirt Bike Test); Keefer runs 14 psi in Pirellis.
Flash 2024 bikes to the 2025 ECU spec at a dealer (Keefer, Vital).
Buy Torx T-handles; consider Works Connection oil cap and Acerbis footpeg hinge covers (MXA).
Exhaust: FMF 4.1 + Megabomb is the only independently ride-tested aftermarket system found (Keefer).
gaps: No dyno-measured results for any aftermarket exhaust (FMF, Pro Circuit, Akrapovic, Yoshimura RS-12 listing seen at a retailer but no test).
No part numbers reported by any source for TF aftermarket parts.
No independent tests found for the 2026 TF 250-X update or TF 250-C.
No Triumph factory team (SMX/MXGP) bike-build feature with parts list found within budget.

No Vital MX forum owner threads surfaced; no forum findings recorded.
